line: Decisions card, lower half, about 72 percent of image height
title: Public dashboard image names an organization in a client renewal context
what: The public screenshot displays a named organization with a renewal deadline and a statement that the user told the desk about it. The value is not reproduced here.
why: The brief's public-image rule forbids naming an employer, client, or person. A client-style organization and renewal detail must not remain public. The sample-data label and synthetic fixture origin do not change what a stranger can see.
evidence: Local OCR located the organization and deadline in the Decisions card. The same organization is seeded by src/agentdesk/server/demo_data.py:82,264,463-472. tools/brand_leak.py:27-40 scans only presentation pack roots, not README PNGs, and its committed denylist is empty.
fix: Replace the public PNG with a recapture from a public-safe fixture containing no organization or person names and no client-style renewal detail. Review the replacement image before committing.

title: Replacement naming guard passes while shipped naming still uses the old product name
what: The patch removes the case-insensitive retired-working-name walk and replaces it with two exact positive assertions. It no longer guards live source, build scripts, operations guides, demo script, or frontend manifest against the retired working name.
why: A green naming test now means only that two strings exist. It passes while executable metadata and other live surfaces keep the old product name.
evidence: The compare patch deletes RETIRED_NAME and the negative walk. At 0f622e3, scripts/build_bundle.py:120-122 passes the old name to Nuitka Windows product, company, and description flags, and line 239 records it as the manifest product. frontend/src/dashboard/Rail.tsx:81-134 renders the old wordmark. The new assertions read neither.
fix: Keep the positive canonical-name tests and restore a scoped negative walk for the retired working name across live shipped surfaces. Add explicit bundle product and company metadata assertions. Define rename exceptions separately instead of deleting the walk.

title: Frontend prerequisite omits the incompatible Node version boundary
what: The quick start says frontend development tools require Node but gives no minimum. The pinned Vite dependency requires Node ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0.
why: A developer with an older Node 20 or Node 22 installation can follow every command and still fail during install or build.
evidence: frontend/package.json:32 pins Vite 7.3.8. frontend/node_modules/vite/package.json:56-58 declares ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0. .github/workflows/enterprise.yml:105-108 uses Node 22.
fix: State the exact supported Node range in the README and consider adding an engines field to frontend/package.json.

title: Absolute keychain claim has supported plaintext exceptions
what: The README and architecture drawing say model keys live in the OS keychain and SQLite keeps only masked hints. That is the normal saved-connection path, not every supported path.
why: A reader could put a key in the documented text configuration or use a machine without a keychain while believing the key cannot exist in plaintext.
evidence: src/agentdesk/config.py:18-38,41-60 accepts every nonempty AGENTDESK_ key, including the model-key environment name. tests/test_config.py:35-37 confirms that acceptance. src/agentdesk/keys/migrate.py:120-136 leaves a legacy secret in the settings row when no usable keychain exists. docs/known-limitations.md:73-77 documents the fallback. No secret value is reproduced here.
fix: Qualify the keychain claim and warn beside the config-file instructions that environment or text-file configuration and the legacy no-keychain fallback can retain plaintext outside SQLite's masked-hint field.

title: Screenshot capture command omits the Playwright browser prerequisite
what: The command installs the Playwright Python package through uv but never installs a Chromium browser binary. On a fresh machine without a cached browser, the audit cannot launch Chromium.
why: The document presents this as the command for replacing public images. A reader can install every listed Python package and still be unable to reproduce the screenshots.
evidence: tools/layout_audit.py:1399 and 3602 call playwright.chromium.launch(headless=True) without an executable path or channel. The documented uv line lists only playwright, keyring, and cryptography. Installing the Python package does not install its browser binary.
fix: Add a browser installation step such as python -m playwright install chromium before the audit and name any operating-system prerequisites.
